CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presents with left shoulder pain for the past week. Pain began during a gymnastics class when patient overextended her left shoulder during a gymnastics move. Patient reports pain with any movement of the left shoulder. She attempted self-treatment with acetaminophen (Tylenol) for 2-3 days without significant relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses left shoulder pain with movement. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Previous surgery on left arm

MEDICATIONS
Acetaminophen (Tylenol) - used for 2-3 days with minimal relief

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in gymnastics classes

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient demonstrates pain with movement of the left shoulder in multiple directions. Examination otherwise unremarkable.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Assessment: Left shoulder joint injury without fracture

Plan:
1. Ibuprofen 600mg orally three times daily for one week
2. Rest left arm for 3-4 weeks, avoiding heavy lifting and weight-bearing activities
3. Use right hand for activities during recovery period
4. Apply ice or heat pad as needed for pain relief
5. Alternative NSAIDs (Advil or Aleve) available if needed
6. Follow-up appointment in 3 weeks to reassess symptoms
7. Repeat imaging may be considered at follow-up if pain persists
8. Instruct patient to contact office if symptoms worsen or do not improve before scheduled follow-up
